raw.explanation: Nitrofurazone is a nitroaromatic prodrug that requires reductive bioactivation by nitroreductase/flavoprotein enzymes to generate cytotoxic hydroxylamine and reactive oxygen species; selectivity likely reflects the expression or activity of such nitroreductases and/or the hypoxic/oxidative-stress state of the tumor cells. The virtual-cell response showing oxidative-stress genes (TXNRD1, CAT, HSPB1) and the known hypoxic selectivity of nitrofurazone support a mechanism in which cells with high nitroreductive capacity and/or defective oxidative-stress defense are most sensitive. Because the drug is activated by bacterial-type nitroreductases, human homologs such as NQO1 and other NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductases are plausible sensitizing features, while intact antioxidant programs (e.g., KEAP1/NFE2L2 pathway) may be protective.
